cards.title: Be worth + -ing
cards.summary: Significa que algo «vale la pena». Después de worth va un sustantivo o un verbo con -ing.
cards.form: be worth + sustantivo / verbo-ing · it's worth + verbo-ing
uses: Recomendar: The museum is worth visiting.
Valorar un esfuerzo: It's worth the effort.
Valor en dinero: This painting is worth a lot of money.
En negativo: It isn't worth it.

pitfalls.wrong: This book is worth to read.
pitfalls.right: This book is worth reading.
pitfalls.why: Después de worth va -ing, no to + verbo.

pitfalls.wrong: It doesn't worth it.
pitfalls.right: It isn't worth it.
pitfalls.why: Worth no es un verbo: se usa con be (it's worth, it isn't worth).

pitfalls.wrong: This book is worth reading it.
pitfalls.right: This book is worth reading.
pitfalls.why: El objeto ya es el sujeto (this book): no se repite con it después del verbo en -ing.

examples.es: Vale la pena visitar el museo.

cards.title: Used to, be used to y get used to
cards.summary: Used to + verbo habla de hábitos del pasado. Be used to + -ing significa «estar acostumbrado a» y get used to + -ing, «acostumbrarse a».
cards.form: used to + verbo base · be used to + sustantivo / -ing · get used to + sustantivo / -ing
uses: Used to: algo que hacías antes y ya no (I used to live in Lima).
Be used to: algo que ya es normal para ti (I'm used to working at night).
Get used to: el proceso de acostumbrarse (You'll get used to the cold).
En be used to y get used to, to es preposición: después va -ing.

pitfalls.wrong: I am used to work at night.
pitfalls.right: I am used to working at night.
pitfalls.why: En be used to, to es preposición: va seguido de -ing.

pitfalls.wrong: I use to play soccer when I was a kid.
pitfalls.right: I used to play soccer when I was a kid.
pitfalls.why: En oraciones afirmativas, el hábito pasado es used to (con -d).

pitfalls.wrong: Did you used to live here?
pitfalls.right: Did you use to live here?
pitfalls.why: Con did se usa use to (sin -d).

pitfalls.wrong: I can't accustom to the weather.
pitfalls.right: I can't get used to the weather.
pitfalls.why: «Acostumbrarse a» algo se dice get used to.

examples.en: I used to live in Lima.
examples.es: Antes vivía en Lima.

examples.en: She didn't use to like coffee.
examples.es: Antes no le gustaba el café.

examples.en: I'm used to working at night.

examples.en: It took me a month to get used to driving on the left.
examples.es: Me tomó un mes acostumbrarme a manejar por la izquierda.

cards.title: Tercer condicional
cards.summary: Imagina un pasado diferente y su resultado, también en el pasado: If I had known, I would have called you (si lo hubiera sabido, te habría llamado).
cards.form: if + had + participio, would have + participio
uses: Lamentos sobre el pasado: If I had studied more, I would have passed.
Reproches: If you had left earlier, you wouldn't have missed the train.
Could have o might have en lugar de would have para algo solo posible: we could have won.
La forma corta 'd es had en la parte del if y would en el resultado: If I'd known, I'd have come.

pitfalls.wrong: If I would have known, I would have called you.
pitfalls.right: If I had known, I would have called you.
pitfalls.why: En la parte del if no va would: se usa had + participio.

pitfalls.wrong: If I had known, I would called you.
pitfalls.right: If I had known, I would have called you.
pitfalls.why: El resultado lleva would have + participio; no se puede quitar have.

pitfalls.wrong: If I knew it yesterday, I would have helped you.
pitfalls.right: If I had known it yesterday, I would have helped you.
pitfalls.why: Para un pasado imaginario se usa had + participio (had known), no el pasado simple.

pitfalls.wrong: If you had told me, I would of come.
pitfalls.right: If you had told me, I would have come.
pitfalls.why: Would've suena como would of, pero se escribe would have.

examples.en: If I had known about the party, I would have gone.
examples.es: Si hubiera sabido de la fiesta, habría ido.

examples.en: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the flight.
examples.es: Si hubiéramos salido antes, no habríamos perdido el vuelo.

examples.en: She would have passed the exam if she had studied harder.
examples.es: Habría aprobado el examen si hubiera estudiado más.

examples.en: What would you have done if you had lost your passport?

examples.en: If it hadn't rained, we could have played outside.
examples.es: Si no hubiera llovido, podríamos haber jugado afuera.

cards.title: Condicionales mixtos
cards.summary: Mezclan tiempos: un pasado diferente con un resultado en el presente (If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now), o una situación presente con un resultado pasado.
cards.form: if + had + participio, would + verbo (pasado → presente) · if + pasado simple, would have + participio (presente → pasado)
uses: Pasado imaginario con resultado ahora: If I had taken that job, I would live in Canada now.
Situación actual con resultado en el pasado: If I weren't so shy, I would have talked to her.
Palabras como now, today o still suelen marcar que el resultado es presente.

pitfalls.wrong: If I had studied medicine, I would have been a doctor now.
pitfalls.right: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
pitfalls.why: Con now, el resultado es presente: would + verbo, no would have.

pitfalls.wrong: If I would speak French, I would have gotten the job.
pitfalls.right: If I spoke French, I would have gotten the job.
pitfalls.why: En la parte del if no va would; una situación presente se expresa con el pasado simple.

pitfalls.wrong: If I didn't miss the bus, I would be home now.
pitfalls.right: If I hadn't missed the bus, I would be home now.
pitfalls.why: El pasado imaginario va con had + participio.

examples.en: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
examples.es: Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora sería médico.

examples.en: If we hadn't missed the bus, we would be home by now.
examples.es: Si no hubiéramos perdido el autobús, ya estaríamos en casa.

examples.en: If she weren't so shy, she would have spoken to him.
examples.es: Si no fuera tan tímida, le habría hablado.

examples.en: If I spoke Italian, I would have understood the movie.
examples.es: Si hablara italiano, habría entendido la película.

examples.en: I wouldn't be so tired if I had gone to bed earlier.
examples.es: No estaría tan cansado si me hubiera acostado más temprano.

cards.title: Wish e if only
cards.summary: Expresan deseos y lamentos: wish + pasado para el presente (I wish I had more time) y wish + had + participio para el pasado (I wish I hadn't said that).
cards.form: wish / if only + pasado simple (presente) · + had + participio (pasado) · + would + verbo (quejas)
uses: Deseos sobre el presente: I wish I lived near the beach. (ojalá viviera…)
Lamentos sobre el pasado: I wish I hadn't eaten so much. (ojalá no hubiera…)
Quejas por lo que hace otra persona: I wish you would stop talking. (ojalá dejaras de…)
If only significa lo mismo, con más intensidad: If only I had more time!

pitfalls.wrong: I wish I have more time.
pitfalls.right: I wish I had more time.
pitfalls.why: Después de wish, el presente se expresa con el pasado: had, no have.

pitfalls.wrong: I wish I didn't say that yesterday.
pitfalls.right: I wish I hadn't said that yesterday.
pitfalls.why: Para lamentar algo del pasado se usa had + participio.

pitfalls.wrong: I wish I would be taller.
pitfalls.right: I wish I were taller.
pitfalls.why: Wish + would sirve para quejarse de lo que hace otra persona, no para uno mismo; con be, usa were (o was).

pitfalls.wrong: I hope I had a car.
pitfalls.right: I wish I had a car.
pitfalls.why: Hope es para algo posible (I hope you pass); wish, para algo imposible o poco probable.

examples.en: I wish I had more free time.
examples.es: Ojalá tuviera más tiempo libre.

examples.en: I wish I lived closer to my family.
examples.es: Ojalá viviera más cerca de mi familia.

examples.en: She wishes she hadn't sold her car.
examples.es: Ella desearía no haber vendido su auto.

examples.en: If only we had left earlier!
examples.es: ¡Si tan solo hubiéramos salido antes!

examples.en: I wish you would stop making that noise.
examples.es: Ojalá dejaras de hacer ese ruido.

examples.en: I wish I were taller.
examples.es: Ojalá fuera más alto.

cards.title: Should have, could have y would have
cards.summary: Modal + have + participio habla del pasado: lo que debería haber pasado (should have), lo que era posible (could have) y lo que habría pasado (would have).
uses: Lamentos y reproches: I should have studied more. You shouldn't have shouted.
Una posibilidad que no se aprovechó: We could have taken a taxi. (podríamos haber tomado)
Un resultado imaginado: I would have helped you, but I didn't know.
Al hablar suenan como should've, could've y would've.

pitfalls.wrong: I should studied more.
pitfalls.right: I should have studied more.
pitfalls.why: Para el pasado, should va con have + participio.

pitfalls.wrong: You should have came earlier.
pitfalls.right: You should have come earlier.
pitfalls.why: Después de have va el participio (come), no el pasado (came).

pitfalls.wrong: I must have called you, sorry.
pitfalls.right: I should have called you, sorry.
pitfalls.why: Para decir debería haber (reproche o lamento) se usa should have; must have es una deducción (seguramente).

pitfalls.wrong: We could of won.
pitfalls.right: We could have won.
pitfalls.why: Could've suena como could of, pero se escribe could have.

examples.en: I should have brought an umbrella.
examples.es: Debería haber traído un paraguas.

examples.en: You shouldn't have spent so much money.
examples.es: No deberías haber gastado tanto dinero.

examples.en: We could have taken a taxi, but we walked.
examples.es: Podríamos haber tomado un taxi, pero caminamos.

examples.en: I would have called you, but my phone died.
examples.es: Te habría llamado, pero se me descargó el teléfono.

examples.en: She could have been a great singer.
examples.es: Podría haber sido una gran cantante.

cards.title: Deducciones sobre el pasado: must have, might have, can't have
cards.summary: Para deducir qué pasó: must have (seguramente), might / may / could have (quizás) y can't / couldn't have (es imposible que).
cards.form: must / might / may / could / can't / couldn't + have + participio
uses: Casi seguro: She must have missed the bus. (seguramente perdió el autobús)
Posible: They might have gotten lost. (quizás se perdieron)
Imposible: He can't have finished already. (no puede ser que ya haya terminado)
Es el pasado de must, might y can't para deducir (B1).

pitfalls.wrong: She must missed the train.
pitfalls.right: She must have missed the train.
pitfalls.why: Para deducir algo del pasado se usa must have + participio.

pitfalls.wrong: They might have get lost.
pitfalls.right: They might have gotten lost.
pitfalls.why: Después de have va el participio: gotten en inglés americano, no get.

pitfalls.wrong: You can't have saw him.
pitfalls.right: You can't have seen him.
pitfalls.why: Have va con el participio (seen), no con el pasado (saw).

examples.en: The streets are wet. It must have rained last night.
examples.es: Las calles están mojadas. Seguramente llovió anoche.

examples.en: She isn't answering. She might have left her phone at home.
examples.es: No contesta. Quizás dejó el teléfono en casa.

examples.en: He can't have finished the report already. It's very long.
examples.es: No puede ser que ya haya terminado el informe. Es muy largo.

examples.en: They're late. They may have gotten lost.
examples.es: Llegan tarde. Puede que se hayan perdido.

examples.en: You must have been very tired after the trip.
examples.es: Debes de haber estado muy cansado después del viaje.

cards.title: Pasiva con verbos de opinión: it is said that…
cards.summary: Para contar lo que la gente dice o cree sin decir quién: It is said that… o He is said to…, muy común en las noticias.
cards.form: It is said / believed / thought / reported + that + oración · sujeto + is said / believed + to + verbo (to have + participio para el pasado)
uses: Noticias y rumores: It is believed that the fire started in the kitchen.
Con la persona como sujeto: He is said to be very rich. (dicen que es muy rico)
Para algo anterior: She is believed to have left the country. (se cree que se fue del país)
Verbos típicos: say, believe, think, report, expect, know.

pitfalls.wrong: Is said that he is very rich.
pitfalls.right: It is said that he is very rich.
pitfalls.why: La oración necesita sujeto: It is said that…, nunca Is said that.

pitfalls.wrong: He is said that he is very rich.
pitfalls.right: He is said to be very rich.
pitfalls.why: Con la persona como sujeto se usa to + verbo, no that.

pitfalls.wrong: She is believed to leave the country last year.
pitfalls.right: She is believed to have left the country last year.
pitfalls.why: Para algo que ya pasó se usa to have + participio.

examples.en: It is believed that the fire started in the kitchen.
examples.es: Se cree que el incendio empezó en la cocina.

examples.en: The singer is said to be very shy.
examples.es: Dicen que el cantante es muy tímido.

examples.en: It is reported that ten people were hurt.
examples.es: Se informa que diez personas resultaron heridas.

examples.en: The thieves are thought to have escaped by car.
examples.es: Se cree que los ladrones escaparon en auto.

examples.en: It is expected that prices will rise again.
examples.es: Se espera que los precios vuelvan a subir.

examples.en: He is known to be a great cook.
examples.es: Se sabe que es un gran cocinero.

cards.title: Have / get something done
cards.summary: Se usa cuando otra persona hace algo por ti, normalmente un servicio: I had my hair cut (me corté el pelo en la peluquería).
cards.form: have / get + objeto + participio (have my car repaired)
uses: Servicios: I'm having my car repaired. We got the house painted.
Get es más informal que have: You should get your eyes checked.
Cosas malas que te pasan: She had her phone stolen. (le robaron el teléfono)
Funciona en todos los tiempos: I'll have it fixed tomorrow.

pitfalls.wrong: I cut my hair at the hairdresser's yesterday.
pitfalls.right: I had my hair cut at the hairdresser's yesterday.
pitfalls.why: Si te lo cortó otra persona, se dice have (o get) your hair cut; I cut my hair significa que te lo cortaste tú.

pitfalls.wrong: I had repaired my car.
pitfalls.right: I had my car repaired.
pitfalls.why: El objeto va antes del participio: have + my car + repaired.

pitfalls.wrong: We're going to have the house paint.
pitfalls.right: We're going to have the house painted.
pitfalls.why: Después del objeto va el participio (painted), no el verbo base.

pitfalls.wrong: I stole my wallet on the bus.
pitfalls.right: I had my wallet stolen on the bus.
pitfalls.why: Para decir me robaron… se usa have + objeto + stolen; I stole significa yo robé.

examples.en: I had my hair cut yesterday.
examples.es: Ayer me corté el pelo (en la peluquería).

examples.en: We're having the kitchen painted next week.
examples.es: La semana que viene nos van a pintar la cocina.

examples.en: You should get your eyes checked.
examples.es: Deberías hacerte revisar la vista.

examples.en: She had her phone stolen on the subway.
examples.es: Le robaron el teléfono en el metro.

examples.en: Where did you get your car repaired?
examples.es: ¿Dónde te arreglaron el auto?

cards.title: Despite, in spite of y whereas
cards.summary: Despite e in spite of (a pesar de) van con un sustantivo o con un verbo en -ing; whereas (mientras que) compara dos hechos opuestos.
cards.form: despite / in spite of + sustantivo o -ing · despite the fact that + oración · oración, whereas + oración
uses: Contraste con un sustantivo: Despite the rain, we went out.
Con un verbo en -ing: In spite of feeling sick, she went to work.
Con una oración completa: despite the fact that it was raining (o simplemente although).
Comparar dos hechos: I love the beach, whereas my sister prefers the mountains.

pitfalls.wrong: Despite of the rain, we went out.
pitfalls.right: Despite the rain, we went out.
pitfalls.why: Despite va sin of; in spite of sí lleva of.

pitfalls.wrong: Despite it was raining, we went out.
pitfalls.right: Despite the rain, we went out.
pitfalls.why: Despite no va con una oración: usa un sustantivo, -ing o although.

pitfalls.wrong: In spite of she was tired, she kept working.
pitfalls.right: In spite of being tired, she kept working.
pitfalls.why: Después de in spite of va -ing o un sustantivo, no sujeto + verbo.

examples.en: Despite the rain, we enjoyed the trip.
examples.es: A pesar de la lluvia, disfrutamos el viaje.

examples.en: In spite of feeling sick, she went to work.
examples.es: A pesar de sentirse mal, fue a trabajar.

examples.en: He didn't get the job despite having a lot of experience.
examples.es: No consiguió el trabajo a pesar de tener mucha experiencia.

examples.en: Despite the fact that it was late, the store was still open.
examples.es: A pesar de que era tarde, la tienda seguía abierta.

examples.en: I prefer coffee, whereas my husband only drinks tea.
examples.es: Yo prefiero el café, mientras que mi esposo solo toma té.
